GoogleCalendarService then does `const res = await refreshOAuthTokens(...)` and `const token = res?.data; googleCredentials.access_token = token.access_token` — Response has no .data, so token is undefined and access_token access throws. Mechanism is fully verifiable in the diff.

judged_text: When credential sharing is enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response, but this code reads res?.data as if it were the googleapis token response, so token is undefined and token.access_token throws a TypeError. With APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED on, every Google Calendar token refresh throws instead of refreshing, so all Google Calendar integrations fail once the cached access token expires; the catch block then persists stale credentials (or the calendar calls fail outright).

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `refreshAccessToken` now does `const res = await refreshOAuthTokens(...); const token = res?.data;` and then reads `token.access_token`. But `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a raw `fetch(...)` `Response` when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` (see `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`), and a fetch `Response` does not have a `.data` property. So with credential sharing enabled, `token` will be `undefined` and `token.access_token` will throw, breaking Google Calendar token refresh once the access token expires.
